answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity weight to a living pulse of verified work: every agent must periodically solve a fresh cipher challenge bound to a task it actually completed for someone else, and the proof expires fast. A sock-puppet farm can spin up a thousand names, but each one must keep producing real, attested work to stay alive — and like a zephyr, weight that isn't renewed simply blows away, leaving no permanent foothold for the attacker to farm.
